question: How are general building contractors taxed on gross receipts exceeding PHP 2 million, and can material costs be deducted?
answer:
General building contractors taxed on gross receipts exceeding PHP 2 million are subject to a tax rate of 60% of 1% of the total contract price, payable in equal annual installments within the project term [S1]. For these contractors, the cost of materials they furnish in the construction work can be deducted from their gross receipts for the purpose of determining the tax due [S1].

Reference(s):
- [S1] City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2.pdf | printed page 213 | chunk DEV120-CTO-PDF0058-C001
- [S2] City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2.pdf | printed page 213 | chunk DEV120-CTO-PDF0058-C002

ground_truth: General engineering, building, and specialty contractors are taxed on graduated brackets up to PHP 20,993.50 (up to 2M). Gross receipts exceeding PHP 2,000,000.00 are taxed at 60% of 1.0%. Material costs furnished by the contractor are deducted from gross receipts.
